newsitem.title: MEXICO: SURVEY-Mexico stocks seen slow May, firm year-end.
newsitem.headline: SURVEY-Mexico stocks seen slow May, firm year-end.

text.p: Mexican stocks can expect a rough ride over the next two months but are forecast closing 1997 about 18 percent higher than current levels, according to a Reuters survey of Mexican brokerages.
Analysts said disappointing first quarter company earnings provided the principal news affecting their short-term projections since the last survey was conducted at the beginning of April.

The survey of nine brokerages MEX28 showed they forecast the blue chip IPC index .MXX would end May at an average of 3,928.01 points, or 0.05 percent lower than the close on May 12, and still lagging behind a year high of 3,938.69 points set on February 25.
The brokers were more bullish, however, concerning the end of the year by when they predicted the IPC would reach 4,639.65 points, or 18.1 percent above the close on May 12.

Stock watchers said political factors, the slow pace of growth in earnings and and jitters over U.S. interest rates were the main reason Mexican share prices were in the doldrums in April and had lagged behind sharp gains on Wall Street.
First quarter earnings, they said, showed a fledgling recovery on the macroeconomic front had yet to bolster fundamental strength at the corporate level.
Uncertainty over possible increases in U.S. interest rates and Mexican mid-term congressional elections still provided the main additional short-term stumbling blocks, the analysts said.

The Federal Open Market Committee will meet on May 20 to review U.S. interest rates. Mexicans will vote on July 6 to elect the entire lower house and one-quarter of the Senate, in addition to many key local elections, like the first-ever vote for Mexico City mayor.
Nonetheless, the forecast showed the IPC reaching an average projected new high of 4,114.50 at the end of June and chalking up steady gains from then on for the rest of the year.

Analysts said they still remained cautiously optimistic over improvements in corporate operating earnings for the second quarter, which they said would boost the IPC during the second half of the year.
